Get the device\'s current date, time, and timezone. Returns an ISO 8601 time string, timezone name, and UTC offset. No parameters required.
Use cases: - Need current timestamp or date - Date formatting or timezone conversion - Calculate time difference

Get hardware and software info of the current device: model, OS version, screen resolution, memory, ABI architecture, etc. No parameters required.
Use cases: - Choose a suitable image resolution based on device capabilities - Determine feature compatibility - Collect device info for troubleshooting

Show structured questions to the user and wait for answers before continuing
UI presentation style. `dialog` is suitable for single-choice / few-question prompts; `bottom_sheet` is suitable for multi-select / multi-text / long forms.
Header title shown at the top of the dialog (optional).
Supplementary text shown above the question list (optional).
Array of questions; see the items schema for per-item details. Common mistakes: omitting `value` from choice `options`, omitting `options` from a choice question, or degrading to plain-text question.

Input type for a single question, controls the picker icon on the right of the input field. Options: text (default, plain text input), time (HH:mm), time_range (HH:mm ~ HH:mm), date (yyyy-MM-dd), date_range (yyyy-MM-dd ~ yyyy-MM-dd), color (#AARRGGBB), city (Province City District), image (system image picker, writes a file:// URI), file (system file picker, writes a file:// URI), folder (system folder picker, writes a file:// URI). System picker results are auto-converted to file:// URIs to avoid SAF permission expiration.

Unified page navigation tool. When the user explicitly asks to open, enter, view, or edit a page/item, call this tool directly. Only deeplinks are accepted, with action=open|edit to decide whether to view or enter the edit flow. Edit confirmation is handled directly by the client; no additional model follow-up questions or multi-round tool calls are required. The tool result returns a reusable deeplink for reopening later.

Add one or more entries (expense/income/excluded) to the ledger

Add entries to the ledger. Supports both single-entry params and a records array for batch insert. amount is in yuan and is auto-converted to cents with 2 decimals. type accepts expense / income / excluded; category is matched by name; on mismatch the result returns an error and lists the available categories. Query, create, import endgame/opening, import game records, delete and export Chinese chess games
Action type: list / detail / create / import_fen / import_json / delete / export
Game ID (required for detail / delete / export)
Whether to create a human-vs-AI game with AI playing red (optional for create, default false)
Export format: fen / json / both (optional for export, default both)

FEN notation string (required for import_fen). Used to import an endgame or a custom opening. Format: "position side halfmove-count fullmove-count", e.g. "rnbakabnr/9/1c5c1/p1p1p1p1p/9/9/P1P1P1P1P/1C5C1/9/RNBAKABNR w 0 1". The position part is 10 rows separated by `/`, each row 9 columns; uppercase = Red (K=General A=Advisor B=Elephant N=Horse R=Chariot C=Cannon P=Pawn), lowercase = Black (k=a b=n r=c p), digits = empty squares.

JSON game record string (required for import_json). Used to import a full game with move replay. Format: {"version":1,"title":"title","initialFen":"initial FEN","result":"result","moves":[{"move":"a0a1","moveCn":"炮二平五"},...]}. `move` is UCCI coordinate format (e.g. a0a1 means move from a0 to a1); `moves` is replayed in order.
